research_question: Under what economic, institutional and psychological conditions does automation of cognitive output weaken incentives to learn, and could the result be high systemic capability with declining distributed human expertise?
assumptions_and_limits: PISA 2025 observations do not identify effects caused by AI adoption and national trends differ.
OECD tertiary wage premia are observed associations, not causal estimates of any individual degree's return.
AI tutoring trials involve different interventions and populations and cannot be averaged as a single effect.
Survey-based cognitive effort and small exploratory EEG evidence do not demonstrate population-wide deterioration or neurological harm.
Technological Dark Age is a conditional scenario, not a factual prediction.
ILO and IMF occupational exposure estimates use different frameworks and do not measure job losses.
counterfactuals: High AI adoption alongside sustained gains in independently tested learning would weaken the central education mechanism.
Firms could automate routine tasks while creating new, better supervised routes to expertise.
Accessible pedagogically designed AI could reduce learning gaps rather than widen them.
Persistent educational wage premia and robust curiosity contradict claims that formal learning has lost all value.

producer_checks.content_depth: EN roughly 5,877 whitespace-delimited words, PT-BR roughly 6,175; 17 substantive analytical sections plus references in both locales.
producer_checks.bilingual_visuals: Two source-based PISA 2025 charts (minimum mathematics proficiency; school perceived as waste of time), two comparable tables, and a causal flow in both locales.
producer_checks.sources: 16 numbered primary or institutional references in each language, covering OECD, UNESCO, ILO, IMF, Stanford, NBER, Microsoft Research, peer-reviewed educational trial and a 2026 working paper; classical works listed separately.
producer_checks.source_date: Historical bibliographic references differentiated from 2024–2026 empirical evidence. PISA 2025 released September 2026, tutoring negative trial October 2026.
producer_checks.falsification: Explicit disconfirming evidence for the technological-dark-age hypothesis and three conditional 2027–2040 pathways.
producer_checks.images: No unverified illustrations or decorative imagery.

contrary_evidence: PISA 2025 Brazilian students report curiosity and effort near OECD mean, and fewer perceive school as a waste of time; an aggregate collapse of interest is not established.
Pedagogically structured AI tutoring can improve learning in controlled settings; effects differ from systems integrated without prescribed pedagogy.
Education remains associated with substantial earnings premiums; occupational task exposure is not observed mass unemployment.
limitations: Full repository-local npm validation and build could not be run because github.com DNS is unavailable in the execution container; GitHub Actions validation remains a separate production gate.
Source cross-check covers central numerical and causal claims; not every historical bibliographic entry was independently recovered in full text.
One central negative educational trial is an October 2026 working paper, not a peer-reviewed settled consensus.
Metaphor of a technological Dark Age is a falsifiable conditional scenario, not a verified present event or deterministic forecast.

en.title: The Age of Disinterest: Artificial Intelligence, the Abandonment of Effort and the Prospect of a New Dark Age
en.deck: A historical, philosophical, psychological and political-economic investigation of what happens to education, human agency, apprenticeship, democracy and inequality when machines deliver the result without the learning process.
en.regime: Rapid automation of cognitive output with uncertain consequences for human learning, skills and autonomy
en.key_risk: Confusing competent machine-generated outputs with genuine learning and confusing weak educational performance with an empirically demonstrated loss of interest
watch: Returns to formal and technical education
Algorithmic public decisions and appeal rights
en.search_text: The Age of Disinterest explores the prospect of AI lowering incentives to learn, outsourcing thought, education and university value, cognitive inequality and technological dark age scenarios.

pt-BR.title: A era do desinteresse: a inteligência artificial, o abandono do esforço e a possibilidade de uma nova Idade das Trevas
pt-BR.deck: Investigação histórica, filosófica, psicológica e de economia política sobre educação, autonomia, aprendizagem profissional, democracia e desigualdade quando as máquinas entregam resultados sem exigir o processo de aprender.
pt-BR.regime: Automação acelerada de tarefas cognitivas com efeitos incertos sobre aprendizagem, competências e autonomia
pt-BR.key_risk: Confundir resultados convincentes gerados pela máquina com aprendizagem efetiva e confundir mau desempenho escolar com perda de interesse empiricamente demonstrada
watch: Retenção sem IA após uso de assistentes
Retornos da formação universitária e técnica
Direito de contestar decisões públicas automatizadas
pt-BR.search_text: A Era do Desinteresse examina IA e incentivos para aprender, terceirização do pensamento, valor da universidade e da escola, desigualdade cognitiva e cenários de uma Idade das Trevas tecnológica.
